instructions: Pat the 1.25 lb beef dry with paper towels and sprinkle 1 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper over it.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large heavy pot over medium high heat. Add half the beef with room between the pieces and leave it until the underside is deep brown, about 3 minutes. Turn the pieces and brown the other sides, about 4 minutes. Transfer them to a plate and brown the rest the same way.

Put all the beef back in the pot and pour in 6 cups water. Peel the onion, cut it in half and add it with the bay leaf, the cinnamon stick and the 1/4 tsp cloves. Scrape up the browned bits from the bottom and bring it to a boil. Skim off the foam that rises.
Turn the heat to low, set the lid on a little ajar and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, until a piece of beef breaks apart easily with a fork.
Meanwhile, peel the carrots and cut them into 1/2 inch cubes.
Pick the leaves off the cilantro and chop them. Set 2 tbsp aside for the top.
Peel the 6 garlic cloves and chop them on a board with 1/2 tsp of the salt. Press and scrape them with the flat of the knife until they turn into a paste.

When the beef is tender, lift it out with a slotted spoon into a bowl. Pour the broth through a strainer into a large bowl and throw away the onion and spices. That should be about 4 cups. Add water if it's short.
Start the rice. Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the 1/3 cup broken vermicelli and stir the whole time until it's golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes. Watch it. It darkens fast.

Add the rice and stir for 1 minute to coat it. Pour in 2 1/2 cups water and the last 1/2 tsp salt and bring it to a boil. Turn the heat to low, cover and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and keep the lid on until you serve.
Wipe out the big pot and heat the last 2 tbsp oil in it over medium heat. Add the carrots and cook, stirring, for 3 minutes.
Add the chopped cilantro (not the 2 tbsp you set aside) and the garlic paste. Stir for about 1 minute, until it smells fragrant. Don't let the garlic brown.
Add the 3 tbsp tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until it turns a shade darker.
Pour in the broth and stir until the paste dissolves. Add the frozen peas and the beef and bring it to a simmer.
Turn the heat to medium low and simmer, uncovered, for 20 minutes, until the carrots are tender and the sauce has thickened a little.
Stir in the 1/2 tsp coriander and the last 1/4 tsp pepper and cook for 1 minute.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
Cut the rest of the lemon into wedges. Fluff the rice with a fork. Serve the stew over the vermicelli rice with the cilantro you set aside on top and the lemon wedges on the side.
method_notes: All three build a tomato paste stew of beef, carrots and peas with garlic, and serve it over rice cooked with toasted vermicelli. Simply Lebanese cooks the beef first in water with onion, bay, cinnamon and cloves to make its own broth, fries garlic and cilantro before the carrots, and adds ground coriander at the end; Alphafoodie sears the beef and uses canned crushed tomatoes; The Matbakh adds potatoes and serves it with lemon. This follows Simply Lebanese's broth and seasoning, sears the beef first the way the other two do, simmers on the stove for 1 hour 15 minutes where the lead uses a pressure cooker, and puts the carrots in before the garlic so the garlic doesn't burn. It's a long cook, about 2 hours 25 minutes in all.
